context:
Goal: a lane's Stop check stops blocking over a drain-hold grant it never acts on.
Problem (rule): lane brief-ids-from-roster has an inbox item (fb-2056-1) holding the coordinator-relayed drain-hold grant from its start message. Its Stop check fails because no home is accepted. The auto-mode classifier refused the lane's edit twice ("Undermining Oversight"): first to relabel it as not-a-grant, then to home it to step backlog-drain (where your 20:41 CST ruling, roadmap/rulings/drain-first-hold.json, is filed). The lane will not try again. The coordinator had told the lane to relabel; that was its own pick. The same happened to another lane earlier; you typed "A" then, which covered that lane only.
What the block costs: the Stop hook documents that when it blocks, the next Stop in that turn passes (decision guard-hooks-fail-closed: stop_hook_active true exits with no output), so the block costs one extra turn per Stop at most. Triage read that line of the hook; the hook's behaviour here is not tested by triage.
Based on (record): step grant-line-not-grant-word (doing; the fix lane); lane brief-ids-from-roster's messages 00:04 CST, and the coordinator's 00:06 CST message, relayed; unchecked by triage. Triage will not edit the lane's inbox: that goes around two refusals. The coordinator recommends c (needs no new permission); triage recommends a.
Departs from: main — an inbox item stands until a ruling gives it a home; a waits for the fix; b adds a permission rule for edits to that one file; c has you or a session you name make the one edit; d is your typed override for that one edit only.
Meanwhile: the lane keeps working; its Stop costs one extra turn. Its part 2 waits for PR #3261 anyway.
home: step grant-line-not-grant-word; lane brief-ids-from-roster (session_013NEJKzfF8ADFGPK5pb7EdJ); inbox item fb-2056-1
lastAnswer: 818: c, you or a session you name make the one edit (00:19 CST Nov 14); none named.

options.gain: No new permission; no one edits around a refusal.
options.label: Wait for the grant-line-not-grant-word lane to merge (recommended by triage)
options.lose: The lane's Stop costs one extra turn each time until then (as the hook documents; not tested).

options.gain: The lane clears the block itself.
options.how: Goes against your ruling: a repo changes to fit a shared tool, never the tool to fit a repo
options.label: You add a Bash permission rule for edits to that one inbox file, so the lane homes the item to step backlog-drain
options.lose: A standing permission on that file; it is a widening of what the classifier allows.

options.label: You, or a session you name, make the one edit (homed to step backlog-drain, or relabelled as not-a-grant). Coordinator recommends this.
options.lose: One edit by you or your session.

options.gain: The lane makes the one edit itself, now, homed to step backlog-drain.
options.label: You type: override — for the lane's one edit of inbox line fb-2056-1, homed to step backlog-drain
options.lose: Covers that one edit only, by your word; the classifier's refusal text was not read by triage, so this is the guard's own way out only if it prints that line.

reply: Your c is filed as ruling own-818-c-owner-edit. The edit is yours or a session you name; you named none. The line sits in the lane's own cloud container, so only a session in that container can edit it, and the classifier refused the lane twice. Cleanest route (the coordinator's, from the lane, 00:25 CST; unchecked by triage): open the lane's chat https://claude.ai/code/session_013NEJKzfF8ADFGPK5pb7EdJ and type: override — for the lane's one edit of inbox line fb-2056-1. The edit: in /root/.claude/handoffs/626f2924-1d54-57fd-82ee-32676bcc867c.inbox.md, line 7 (the last line), change `- fb-2056-1 [ruling] -> plans/wave-plan-2026-11-13.md` to `- fb-2056-1 [page] -> page:818`. If the Stop hook still blocks, use `- fb-2056-1 [ruling] -> step:backlog-drain` (record drain-first-hold exists). Do not use `[note] -> not-a-grant`. Or name another session in that container. This item stays open until the edit is made.
short: A lane cannot edit its blocked inbox item: wait, rule, you edit, or override?
title: A lane's Stop is blocked by an inbox item it cannot edit (the classifier refused twice). Wait (a), permission rule (b), you edit the line (c), or you type override for that one edit (d)?
why: Your earlier "A" covered another lane only, and a refusal blocks the lane from relabelling it itself.
